project_type: Python CLI security toolkit for bug bounty researchers
build_system: pip with requirements.txt, pure Python standard library + colorama
test_framework: No formal test framework; verification via running the tools and checking output
test_command: python -m monster --help && python -m monster --target example.com --module recon --dry-run -o /tmp/monster-test
verification_instructions: 1. Ensure 'python -m monster --help' shows all CLI options. 2. Run a quick scan against a safe target to confirm modules load and produce output. 3. Verify all imports work without errors.
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET - full network access available. Python 3.11 default. All networking done via urllib/socket (no requests library). Must be thread-safe. Rate limiting required on all network calls.
contribution_requirements: Pure Python standard library + colorama only. No active exploitation. Proper User-Agent and rate limiting on all requests. Graceful error handling for timeouts and connection failures.
key_patterns: The existing analyze.py uses: dataclasses for data structures, colorama for output, argparse for CLI, urllib.request for HTTP, socket for DNS, json for serialization, concurrent patterns with threading. Follow the same color scheme (C_RED, C_YEL, C_GRN, C_CYN, C_MAG, C_WHT, C_RST, C_BLD).
directory_structure: Bug-Bounty/ contains apk_analyzer/ (existing tool). New monster/ package will be created alongside it with: __init__.py, main.py, recon.py, js_analyzer.py, vuln_scanner.py, report_generator.py, config.py, utils.py, wordlists/subdomains.txt, and __main__.py for CLI entry point.
